title: 🌍 UNIT 2: CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Climate change → long-term changes in the Earth's climate system.

⭐ Climate change affects temperature, rainfall, sea level, ice, ecosystems, agriculture and human societies.

title: 🌡️ 2.1 BASIC CONCEPTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Climate → atmospheric conditions of a place over many years.

🌤️ Weather → atmospheric condition at a particular time or short period.

🌍 Regional climate → climate of a particular region, such as the Horn of Africa.

🌎 Global climate → average climate of the entire world.

🔄 Climate change → persistent change in the mean and/or variability of climate properties over decades or longer.

🔥 Global warming → long-term increase in Earth's average temperature.

⭐ A single unusually hot or cold day is not enough to establish climate change; long-term patterns are important.

title: 🌱 2.1.1 GREENHOUSE EFFECT & GREENHOUSE GASES
notes:
Greenhouse gases (GHGs) trap heat in the atmosphere and help maintain Earth's temperature.

Important GHGs →
🔹 Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
🔹 Methane (CH₄)
🔹 Nitrous oxide (N₂O)
🔹 Water vapor

🌿 Natural greenhouse effect → essential for life.

⚠️ Increased concentrations of greenhouse gases from human activities strengthen the warming effect.

⭐ CO₂ remains in the atmosphere for a long time and is strongly associated with modern warming.

title: 📈 2.2 TRENDS IN GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Global climate observations show a long-term warming trend.

🌡️ Global average surface temperature has increased.

🧊 Glaciers and ice sheets → decreasing.

🌊 Sea level → rising.

🌧️ Rainfall patterns → changing in different regions.

🌿 Ecosystems and watersheds → increasingly affected.

⭐ The textbook's IPCC projection indicates that continued high GHG emissions could produce substantial further warming during the 21st century.

title: 🇪🇹 2.2.1 CLIMATE CHANGE IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
Climate change creates important risks for Ethiopia because livelihoods and economic activities depend strongly on climate-sensitive resources.

Major concerns →
🔹 Rising temperatures
🔹 Variable rainfall
🔹 Drought risk
🔹 Flooding and intense rainfall
🔹 Pressure on agriculture and water resources
🔹 Effects on ecosystems and livelihoods

⭐ Climate variability and long-term climate change can interact, increasing vulnerability in climate-sensitive areas.

title: 🌍 2.3 NATURAL & HUMAN-INDUCED CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Climate change can result from both natural processes and human activities.

🔵 Natural causes → changes in solar radiation, atmospheric composition, Earth's surface, volcanic activity and internal ocean-atmosphere circulation.

🔴 Human causes → mainly greenhouse-gas emissions from fossil-fuel burning, deforestation, industry and transport.

⭐ Modern warming over recent decades is strongly associated with human activities.

title: ☀️ 2.3.1 NATURAL CAUSES OF CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Natural climate influences include:

1️⃣ Changes in incoming solar radiation → variations in solar energy reaching Earth.

2️⃣ Changes in Earth's orbit → alter the amount and distribution of solar energy received.

3️⃣ Atmospheric particles → natural aerosols can reflect sunlight and produce cooling effects.

4️⃣ Volcanic eruptions → sulfur-rich aerosols can reduce incoming sunlight and cause temporary cooling.

5️⃣ Ocean-atmosphere circulation → redistributes heat and energy within the climate system.

title: 🛰️ 2.3.2 MILANKOVITCH THEORY
notes:
Milankovitch Theory explains long-term natural climate variations through changes in Earth's orbital and axial movements.

Three major cycles:

🔹 Eccentricity → changes in the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun.

🔹 Precession → wobbling of Earth's rotational axis.

🔹 Obliquity → changes in the tilt of Earth's axis.

⭐ These cycles influence the amount and distribution of solar energy reaching Earth and are associated with glacial and interglacial periods.

title: ☀️ 2.3.3 VARIATIONS IN SOLAR OUTPUT
notes:
The Sun's energy output varies slightly with solar activity.

🔹 Sunspots → dark regions on the Sun associated with strong magnetic activity.

🔹 Sunspot activity follows cycles of about 11 years.

🔹 Periods with more sunspot activity are associated with slightly greater solar energy output.

⭐ Changes in solar output can contribute to natural climate variations.

title: 🌋 2.3.4 ATMOSPHERIC PARTICLES & VOLCANISM
notes:
Aerosols → tiny solid or liquid particles suspended in the atmosphere.

Natural sources →
🌋 Volcanic eruptions
🔥 Wildfires
💨 Dust storms

🔹 Sulfur-rich volcanic aerosols can reflect sunlight and cool Earth's surface.

⭐ The climatic effect of aerosols depends on their size, composition, color, concentration and position in the atmosphere.

title: 🏭 2.3.5 HUMAN CAUSES OF CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Major human activities increasing greenhouse gases include:

🔥 Burning fossil fuels → electricity, heating and transportation.

🌳 Deforestation → releases stored carbon and reduces carbon absorption.

🏭 Industrial activities → release greenhouse gases and other pollutants.

🚗 Transportation → fossil-fuel combustion produces CO₂.

🌾 Agriculture → contributes methane and nitrous oxide emissions.

🏙️ Urbanization → changes land surfaces and local climate conditions.

⭐ Human activities have become the dominant cause of recent global warming.

title: 🔥 2.3.6 GLOBAL WARMING
notes:
Global warming → long-term rise in Earth's average surface temperature.

Evidence includes:
🔹 Rising global temperatures.
🔹 Melting glaciers and ice sheets.
🔹 Rising sea levels.
🔹 Changing precipitation patterns.
🔹 Changes in growing seasons.
🔹 Changes in ecosystems and species distribution.

⭐ Global warming is a long-term trend, not a single weather event.

title: 🌊 2.4 CONSEQUENCES OF CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Climate change affects natural systems, human health, agriculture, water resources and economies.

Major consequences →
🌡️ Higher temperatures
🌧️ Changing precipitation
🏜️ More drought risk
🌊 Sea-level rise
🧊 Melting ice and snow
🌾 Agricultural impacts
🌳 Ecosystem changes
🦋 Biodiversity loss
🏥 Human health impacts

⭐ Impacts vary between regions depending on climate, geography, ecosystems and vulnerability.

title: 🌡️ 2.4.1 TEMPERATURE & PRECIPITATION IMPACTS
notes:
🌡️ Rising temperatures can increase heat waves and heat-related health problems.

🌧️ Precipitation changes are unevenly distributed.

🔹 Some regions → increased precipitation.
🔹 Other regions → reduced precipitation.
🔹 Heavy precipitation events → may become more intense.
🔹 Lower-latitude regions → may experience more frequent droughts.

⭐ Changes in temperature and rainfall directly affect water availability, agriculture and ecosystems.

title: 🌊 2.4.2 SEA LEVEL, ICE & POLAR REGIONS
notes:
Sea-level rise is associated with warming oceans and loss of land ice.

🧊 Major changes →
🔹 Melting glaciers.
🔹 Shrinking ice sheets.
🔹 Declining Arctic sea ice.
🔹 Rising sea levels.
🔹 Greater coastal flooding risk.

🌍 Polar warming can also change interactions between temperature, precipitation, wind and ice.

⭐ Coastal and island communities are especially vulnerable to sea-level rise.

title: 🌿 2.4.3 EFFECTS ON ECOSYSTEMS
notes:
Climate change can alter ecosystems by changing temperature, water availability and habitat conditions.

🔹 Species may shift their geographic ranges.
🔹 Some species may become more dominant while others decline.
🔹 Wildlife habitats can be lost or altered.
🔹 Forest fires may increase during dry periods.
🔹 Ecosystem health can affect human well-being.

⭐ Climate-driven changes in species distribution can affect food supplies, health and ecosystem services.

title: 🌾 2.4.4 AGRICULTURE & FOOD SECURITY
notes:
Climate change can strongly affect agriculture through changes in temperature, rainfall, drought and growing seasons.

🔹 Crop yields may decline in many tropical and developing regions.
🔹 Water shortages can reduce agricultural productivity.
🔹 Extreme weather can damage crops and livestock.
🔹 Changes in growing seasons can create both opportunities and risks.

⭐ Food security becomes more vulnerable when climate impacts reduce agricultural production.

title: 🏥 2.4.5 EFFECTS ON HUMAN WELL-BEING
notes:
Climate change can affect people directly and indirectly.

🔹 Heat waves → increased heat-related illness and deaths.

🔹 Changing rainfall → affects water supply and food production.

🔹 Ecosystem degradation → affects livelihoods and resources.

🔹 Species distribution changes → can influence disease patterns.

🔹 Extreme events → can damage infrastructure and increase economic losses.

⭐ Climate change affects health, livelihoods, food security and economic development.

title: 🛡️ 2.5 ADAPTATION & MITIGATION STRATEGIES
notes:
Two major responses to climate change:

🛡️ Adaptation → adjusting human, ecological or economic systems to actual or expected climate impacts.

🌱 Mitigation → reducing greenhouse-gas emissions and increasing carbon sinks to limit climate change.

⭐ Adaptation = reduce the harm from impacts.
⭐ Mitigation = reduce the causes of climate change.

title: 🌾 2.5.1 CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION
notes:
Important adaptation strategies in Ethiopia include:

🔹 Soil conservation
🔹 Terracing
🔹 Water harvesting
🔹 Crop diversification
🔹 Changing crop planting dates
🔹 Tree planting
🔹 Irrigation

⭐ Adaptation helps communities reduce vulnerability and cope with changing climatic conditions.

title: 🔄 2.5.2 TYPES OF ADAPTATION
notes:
🔹 Reactive adaptation → occurs after climate impacts become apparent.

🔹 Anticipatory adaptation → occurs before impacts become apparent.

🔹 Public adaptation → driven by government or public interest.

🔹 Private adaptation → undertaken by individuals, households or companies.

🔹 Planned adaptation → deliberate action based on expected or observed climate changes.

🔹 Autonomous adaptation → occurs naturally or independently without a specific policy decision.

title: 🌱 2.5.3 CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION
notes:
Mitigation aims to prevent climate change from becoming more severe by reducing greenhouse-gas emissions and strengthening carbon sinks.

🔹 Reduce fossil-fuel use.
🔹 Expand renewable energy.
🔹 Protect forests.
🔹 Increase afforestation and reforestation.
🔹 Improve energy efficiency.
🔹 Reduce emissions from transport and industry.
🔹 Store carbon in forests, soils and oceans.

⭐ Renewable energy sources → sunlight + wind + water + geothermal heat.

title: 🌍 2.6 INTERNATIONAL CONVENTIONS & AGREEMENTS
notes:
International cooperation is necessary because climate change crosses national boundaries.

Major milestones include:

📅 1979 → First World Climate Conference.
📅 1988 → Toronto Conference on the Changing Atmosphere.
📅 1988 → WMO + UNEP established the IPCC.
📅 1990 → IPCC First Assessment Report.
📅 1992 → international negotiations led to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
📅 1997 → Kyoto Protocol adopted.
📅 2001 → Marrakesh Accords.
📅 2005 → Kyoto Protocol entered into force.

⭐ Main goal → coordinated global action to address climate change.

title: 📜 2.6.1 KEY CLIMATE AGREEMENTS
notes:
🔹 Toronto Conference (1988) → encouraged development of a comprehensive global framework to protect the atmosphere.

🔹 UNFCCC → provides the international framework for cooperation on climate change.

🔹 Kyoto Protocol → established commitments for reducing greenhouse-gas emissions, particularly for developed countries.

🔹 Buenos Aires Plan of Action → advanced negotiations and work on climate-change issues, including adaptation.

🔹 Marrakesh Accords → developed detailed rules for implementing Kyoto-related mechanisms and commitments.

🔹 Paris Agreement → later strengthened international cooperation through national climate commitments.

title: 🇪🇹 2.7 CLIMATE RESILIENT GREEN ECONOMY (CRGE)
notes:
CRGE → Ethiopia's strategy for achieving economic development while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions and strengthening resilience to climate change.

🌱 Main idea → combine economic growth, environmental sustainability and climate resilience.

🔹 The strategy uses a sectoral approach and initially prioritized 60 initiatives.

⭐ Green growth → development that improves livelihoods while limiting environmental damage and emissions.

title: 🌾 2.7.1 CRGE PILLAR 1: AGRICULTURE
notes:
Improving crop and livestock production for higher farmer income and food security while reducing emissions.

🔹 Improve agricultural productivity.
🔹 Reduce soil-based emissions.
🔹 Limit pressure on forests by reducing expansion of cultivated land.
🔹 Improve livestock resource efficiency and productivity.
🔹 Increase pastoralist income while limiting emissions.

⭐ Goal → higher agricultural productivity + food security + lower emissions.

title: 🌳 2.7.2 CRGE PILLAR 2: FORESTS
notes:
Protecting and re-establishing forests for economic and ecosystem services, including carbon storage.

🔹 Reduce demand for fuelwood.
🔹 Increase afforestation.
🔹 Increase reforestation.
🔹 Improve forest management.
🔹 Promote area closure.
🔹 Increase carbon sequestration.

⭐ Forests → provide ecosystem services + store carbon + support economic development.

title: ⚡ 2.7.3 CRGE PILLAR 3: RENEWABLE ENERGY
notes:
Expanding electricity generation from renewable energy for domestic and regional markets.

Ethiopia's major renewable-energy potential includes:

💧 Hydropower
🌋 Geothermal energy
☀️ Solar energy
💨 Wind energy

⭐ Renewable electricity → supports development while producing very low greenhouse-gas emissions.

title: 🚆 2.7.4 CRGE PILLAR 4: ENERGY-EFFICIENT TECHNOLOGY
notes:
Leapfrogging to modern and energy-efficient technologies in transport, industry and buildings.

🔹 Improve energy efficiency.
🔹 Promote alternative fuels.
🔹 Improve transport systems.
🔹 Introduce stricter fuel-efficiency standards.
🔹 Develop electric rail powered by renewable energy.
🔹 Improve efficiency in industries such as cement, textile, leather and fertilizer.

⭐ Goal → modern development with lower energy use and lower emissions.

title: 🧠 UNIT 2 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
🌤️ Weather → short-term atmospheric condition.
🌍 Climate → long-term atmospheric pattern.
🔥 Global warming → long-term increase in average global temperature.
🌡️ Climate change → long-term change in climate characteristics.

🔵 Natural climate change → caused by natural processes.
🔴 Human-induced climate change → strongly influenced by human activities.

🛡️ Adaptation → adjust to climate impacts.
🌱 Mitigation → reduce greenhouse gases and strengthen carbon sinks.

🌳 Carbon sink → system that absorbs and stores carbon.
🏭 Greenhouse gas → gas that absorbs/traps heat in the atmosphere.
